category_title: Students with hyperactive-impulsive behaviors who disrupt classroom instruction
minimal_context: The student is sitting in a regular classroom completing a timed math and spelling worksheet.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please sit at your desk and complete the math and spelling worksheet. You have 15 minutes to finish.

STUDENT: (Constantly shifting in his place and fidgeting with his stationery items) I do not like written work.

TUTOR: Just focus on the paper and keep trying.

STUDENT: (Gets up and starts walking in class, making noises) I want to hurry to finish!

TUTOR: You need to sit down. Your work is incomplete and you are not keeping pace with the other students.

STUDENT: (Pouts and starts crying easily) I can't do it! (Leaves the incomplete work on the desk, looking easily irritated and frustrated)

options.A: Prompt the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the rest of the class for help with the worksheet.
options.B: Make sure not to give the student any attention while he is walking around the classroom.
options.C: Provide a range of different activities within the class period for the student to complete.
options.D: Approach the situation from an affective lens, discuss the benefits of giftedness, and ask if he is satisfied with not utilizing his gift.
